title: LTX-Video official repository
claims: The 0.9.8 release lists 13B dev, 13B distilled, 13B mix, 2B distilled, FP8 variants and a detailer IC-LoRA; distilled checkpoints derive from the same 13B dev base.
The 0.9.7 distilled model recommends 8 or fewer diffusion steps and does not require CFG or STG; the 2B 0.9.6 distilled release is described as 15x faster than the non-distilled model.

The repository documents 1216x704 at 30fps as the new default and says 0.9.8 supports up to 60 seconds; resolution should be divisible by 32 and frames follow 8k+1, with best results below 1280x720 and 257 frames.
Supported controls include multiple keyframes, video extension, video-to-video, IC-LoRA detailer, depth, pose and canny control, plus LoRA training for control/effect adapters.

resources.gpu: H100 example for 0.9.7 distilled; no L4/A100 qualification

measurements.resolution: HD (exact dimensions not stated in the cited line)
measurements.note: Author statement for 0.9.7 distilled HD generation; not a 0.9.8 L4/A100 benchmark.

limitations: The README does not publish L4/A100 peak VRAM, host RAM or paired wall-time. The 10-second H100 statement belongs to 0.9.7, not a controlled 0.9.8 test.

topic: LTX-2.5 official audio-video model and pipelines
title: LTX-2 official Python inference and trainer repository
claims: LTX-2.5 is the recommended model; the quick start downloads a 22B distilled transformer, Gemma 4 12B text encoder, video VAE, audio VAE and spatial upsampler.
The model list distinguishes 22B dev for guided two-stage TI2Vid/Keyframe/A2Vid pipelines from 22B distilled for DistilledPipeline, DFR, ICLoRA and DubIt.
Pipelines include text/image-to-video, video-to-video, keyframe interpolation, audio-to-video, retake, HDR, Dub-It and text-to-audio; audio is a model modality rather than a post-remux-only feature.
The quick start defaults to 121 frames and the DFR example states 1024x1536 at 24fps; UHD 4K is 3840x2176.

resources.gpu: No single-GPU inference qualification in README

limitations: The repository has no L4/A100 inference wall-time or peak VRAM. The 80GB+ and 32GB low-VRAM statements in the linked trainer README concern training, not generation.

topic: LTX-2 pipeline grid, two-stage and audio contracts
title: LTX-2 pipeline reference
claims: DistilledPipeline uses 8 predefined sigmas, 8 steps in stage 1 and 4 in stage 2, with a spatial upsampler and no guidance.
DFR stage 1 is half resolution and stage 2 applies a 2x spatial detailing IC-LoRA; optional temporal rounds double playback fps while preserving approximate wall-clock duration.
DFR final dimensions must be divisible by 64, or by 128 with spatial-upscalings=2; num_frames must be 8k+1. From 121 frames, playback is 24/48/96fps for temporal rounds 0/1/2.
A2Vid takes audio input and returns original waveform; Dub-It uses video/audio reference tokens and matched lip movements/speaker context.
limitations: This is an execution contract and pipeline description, not a hardware benchmark or a claim of identity fidelity outside Dub-It.

title: LTX-2 optimization documentation
claims: Official runtime quantization policies include FP8 cast, FP8 scaled matrix multiplication, NVFP4 cast and NVFP4 prequant.
FP8 cast downcasts linear weights during loading and works without extra dependencies; FP8 scaled MM is aimed at Hopper+ native FP8; NVFP4 requires Blackwell SM>=10 and ltx_kernels.
The docs recommend expandable CUDA segments and CPU/disk offload for memory-constrained or CUDA-graph single-GPU paths.
The docs do not publish absolute VRAM or wall-time figures for these policies.

resources.gpu: FP8 any supported GPU; NVFP4 Blackwell SM>=10

limitations: No L4/A100 measurement, no quality comparison, and NVFP4 is not applicable to L4/A100 hardware.

topic: HunyuanVideo-1.5 official base and distilled versions
title: HunyuanVideo-1.5 official repository
claims: HunyuanVideo-1.5 is an 8.3B T2V/I2V model; official minimum GPU memory is 14GB with model offloading enabled.

The 480p I2V step-distilled checkpoint is recommended at 8 or 12 steps; 4 steps is faster with slightly reduced quality. Official RTX4090 end-to-end claim is within 75 seconds and about 75% faster, but is not an L4/A100 test.
Base, CFG-distilled, step-distilled and SR checkpoints are listed for 480p/720p; command defaults are 121 frames and 50 steps, with 480p/720p resolution choices.
The repo documents CFG distill at 50 steps, 480p I2V step distill at 8/12 steps, 480→720 SR at 6 steps and 720→1080 SR at 8 steps; CPU/group offload and FP8 GEMM options are available.

resources.gpu: Single NVIDIA GPU with CPU/model offload

limitations: No L4/A100 wall-time or peak host RAM. The official 14GB number assumes offload and does not establish a specific L4 execution. No first-party native audio or identity guarantee is documented.

title: Hy1.5-Distill-Models model card
claims: The card publishes 4-step HunyuanVideo-1.5 T2V models: base 16.7GB and scaled FP8 E4M3 8.85GB.
The LightX2V recipe requires infer_steps=4, guidance_scale=1, denoising_step_list [1000,750,500,250], 81 frames, 16fps and 16:9; offload is supported on consumer RTX30/40/50 GPUs.

The author describes 4-step distillation as approximately 25x faster than standard 50-step inference and FP8 as roughly 50% memory reduction; neither has a target L4/A100 wall-time measurement in this card.
The card says current distilled support is 480p and still requires original HunyuanVideo-1.5 structure/weights.

resources.gpu: Consumer RTX30/40/50 stated; no named target GPU

limitations: Speed and memory numbers are author claims without L4/A100 run logs; no quality comparison beyond the claim of maintained quality.

title: HunyuanVideo official repository
claims: The original HunyuanVideo is a 13B model; official peak GPU memory is 60GB for 720x1280x129f and 45GB for 544x960x129f, with an 80GB GPU recommended.
Official single-GPU dimensions include 540p/720p aspect-ratio buckets, each with 129 frames; the example uses 50 inference steps and CPU offload.
Official FP8 weights and scales save about 10GB of GPU memory.
limitations: This model is outside the L4/ A100 40GB low/mid envelope in BF16; FP8 save claim is not an L4 qualification and no native audio is documented.

title: HunyuanVideo GGUF direct conversion
claims: The card is a direct GGUF conversion of tencent/HunyuanVideo for native ComfyUI HunyuanVideo nodes, not a finetune.
The 13B card lists Q3_K_S 6.09GB, Q4_K_S/Q4_0 7.74GB, Q4_K_M 7.88GB, Q5_K_M 9.45GB, Q6_K 11GB, Q8_0 14GB and BF16 25.6GB.
The card gives loader placement and quantization file sizes but no VRAM peak, wall-time or controlled quality comparison.
limitations: File size is not peak VRAM; no L4/A100 output or quality data. It is the original 13B model, not HunyuanVideo-1.5.

topic: FramePack official F1/P1 and low-VRAM contract
title: FramePack official README
claims: FramePack is a next-frame-section model with constant-length context; F1 released 2025-05-03 and P1 anti-drifting/history discretization results are dated June/July 2025.
Official requirements are RTX30/40/50 with FP16/BF16 and at least 6GB GPU memory; a 13B model can generate one minute at 30fps/1800 frames at that floor.
Author speed on RTX4090 is 2.5s/frame unoptimized or 1.5s/frame with TeaCache; laptop RTX3060/3070Ti is 4–8x slower.

For one sanity-check example, the author says about 30% of users obtain the shown typical worse TeaCache result and the other 70% obtain hardware-dependent random results. The page advises full diffusion for final quality. This is not a general quality success-rate measurement.

resources.timing_basis: Calculated from author 1.5s/frame x 1800 frames, not a timed 60-second clip; excluded from measured-latency counts.

limitations: No official L4/A100 measurement or fixed output resolution. 4090/laptop figures cannot be converted into L4 throughput. No native audio claim.

topic: FramePack real failure and slow run evidence
title: FramePack issue #117: RTX 3090 and 64GB RAM slow generation
claims: The issue body logs an RTX3090 run with 24GB VRAM and 64GB RAM; dynamic swap preserves 6GB for the transformer and 8GB for offload.
The logged 512x768 output grows through 33, 69, 105 and 145 frames, with 25 steps per section taking roughly 3:57–4:11 each; the issue title reports about 16 minutes for a 5-second video.

A community reply reports TeaCache plus SageAttention around 10 minutes for 5 seconds, while another RTX3060 report records roughly 7 minutes per generated second; the thread also records missing attention kernels and later ghosting concerns.
limitations: Single issue thread with changing software/kernel setup; no L4/A100 and no controlled quality score. It is evidence of failure/slow path, not a general speed law.

title: FramePack Studio issue #349: on-the-fly NF4 quantization
claims: The fork reports 4-bit NF4 on FramePack F1 and original models, with LoRA support in release 0.5.1; the 8-bit integer option did not work.

Tests on RTX3060 12GB with approximately 7GB free VRAM compare BF16 vs NF4 seconds/iteration at multiple resolutions; at 704x544 with magcache enabled, second-section BF16 is 10.62s/it and NF4 9.82s/it; at 832x640, BF16 15.03 and NF4 15.16s/it.
The author reports ghosting on fast movement, worse at lower resolutions, and says NF4 is loaded fully in VRAM.

resources.workflow: FramePack Studio fork, F1/original, magcache on/off

measurements.note: Second section, magcache on; author reports about 7GB free VRAM needed.

limitations: Community fork and RTX3060 only; no L4/A100, no MP4 quality metric, and lower-bit visual artifacts are explicitly reported.

topic: CogVideoX official versions, memory and timing
title: CogVideo and CogVideoX official README
claims: The latest listed family is CogVideoX1.5-5B and 5B-I2V; older 2B, 5B and 5B-I2V remain available.
CogVideoX1.5 supports 1360x768, 16N+1 frames (default 81), 5 or 10 seconds at 16fps; old 2B/5B family uses 720x480, 8N+1 frames (default 49), 6 seconds at 8fps.
Diffusers memory entries are from 10GB BF16 and 7GB INT8 for 1.5-5B, 5GB BF16 and 4.4GB INT8 for 2B; official A100/H100 timing at 50 steps is about 1000/550s for 1.5-5B and 180/90s for 2B.

Official data explanation says memory tests used A100/H100 optimizations and were not measured on other architectures; INT8 is slower, INT4 is unsupported, and TorchAO/Optimum-Quanto can quantize components.
The repo links I2V, V2V continuation, CogVideoX-ControlNet, interpolation and ConsisID adapters.

resources.gpu: A100/H100 for timing and memory tables
resources.workflow: Diffusers with sequential CPU offload/VAE slicing/tiling

limitations: No L4 measurement; official note limits memory testing to A100/H100. No native audio branch in the official repo; ControlNet/ConsisID are linked derivatives, not base-model guarantees.

title: VideoX-Fun official repository
claims: The repo verifies execution on RTX3060 12GB, RTX3090 24GB, V100 16GB, A10 24GB and A100 40/80GB and asks for about 60GB disk.
GPU memory modes are model_cpu_offload, model_cpu_offload_and_qfloat8 and sequential_cpu_offload; qfloat8 saves more GPU memory with a possible small performance reduction.
CogVideoX-Fun V1.5-5B-InP is trained for 512/768/1024 resolutions, 85 frames at 8fps; V1.1 InP/Pose/Control variants cover 512/768/1024/1280, 49 frames at 8fps.

Official scripts support text-to-video, image-to-video with start/end images, video-to-video, and controlled video generation using Canny, Pose or Depth; model zoo lists MLSD, trajectory and camera-control variants.

resources.workflow: VideoX-Fun Python, WebUI or ComfyUI entry

limitations: No L4/A100 wall-time or peak VRAM table; tested A10 is not L4. No native audio evidence. The resolution/frame claims describe training/output contract, not a quality guarantee.

topic: Mochi-1 official model and memory boundary
title: Genmo Mochi official repository
claims: Mochi 1 is a 10B Apache-2.0 text-to-video model with LoRA training support; official code exposes a MochiSingleGPUPipeline with CPU offload.
The official code example uses height 480, width 848, 31 frames and 64 inference steps; initial release output is 480p.
The repo states approximately 60GB VRAM for single-GPU execution, recommends at least one H100, and says ComfyUI can optimize below 20GB without giving a measurement.
Official limitations include motion warping/distortion in edge cases and poor animated-content performance; no I2V, control or native audio contract is documented.

resources.gpu: Single H100 recommended; single-GPU native path about 60GB

limitations: Official native path is outside low/mid resources; the ComfyUI <20GB statement is unquantified. No L4/A100 generation benchmark, audio or identity guarantee.

title: ComfyUI official Mochi example
claims: The workflow accepts BF16/FP16 files or FP8 files and provides an all-in-one FP8 checkpoint.
ComfyUI says FP8 files can help with memory issues and may be faster on GPUs with FP8 operations, but quality is lower than 16-bit files.

resources.resolution: Mochi workflow; official example has no explicit output table

limitations: No peak VRAM, speed, A100/L4 or output-quality measurement beyond the qualitative FP8 warning.

title: calcuis Mochi GGUF test pack
claims: The card is a GGUF quantized Mochi test pack for ComfyUI GGUF nodes with a workflow JSON.
Files include Mochi Q3_K_M 4.31GB, T5 text encoder Q4_0 2.9GB and Mochi VAE FP8 E4M3 460MB; the card also lists Q4_0 2.9GB, Q8_0 5.06GB and F16 9.53GB.
The author says the revised workflow bypasses OOM and is around 50% faster with the new FP8 VAE file, but supplies no named GPU/time log.
limitations: File sizes and an unqualified speed claim do not establish VRAM or L4/A100 output quality. No native audio/control evidence.

title: Pyramid Flow official repository
claims: The official model has miniFLUX and SD3 variants; miniFLUX supports 384p video up to 5s and 768p video up to 10s, all at 24fps, and supports text-conditioned image-to-video.
CPU offloading allows inference below 12GB GPU memory, and sequential CPU offload below 8GB, with an efficiency penalty.
A single A100 generates a 5s 768p 24fps video in 5.5 minutes; 4 A100s take 2.5 minutes. I2V example uses [10,10,10] inference steps.
Official repo includes DiT fine-tuning code but no control, native audio, quantized model or identity consistency claim.

resources.gpu: Single A100 timing; CPU offload supports lower-memory single GPU

limitations: No L4/A100-40GB split, no host RAM peak, no direct quality score for offload, and no quantized checkpoint evidence.

topic: EasyAnimate V5.1 single GPU matrix and controls
title: EasyAnimate official repository
claims: EasyAnimate V5.1 uses Qwen2-VL text encoding and Flow sampling; it supports bilingual Chinese/English, LoRA/reward training, common control inputs, trajectory control and camera control.
The 12B memory matrix marks 24GB as runnable at 384x672x25/49, 576x1008x25/49 and 768x1344x25, but not 768x1344x49; 40GB and 80GB rows can run all listed sizes.
At 25 steps on A10 24GB, 12B times are approximately 120s/240s/320s/750s for 384x672x25/49 and 576x1008x25/49; A100 80GB times are 45/90/120/300/265/710s across the six listed sizes.
Memory modes are model_cpu_offload, model_cpu_offload_and_qfloat8 and sequential_cpu_offload; sequential offload is slower.
limitations: The 24GB result is A10, not L4. No A100 40GB timing and no native audio. Matrix icons encode offload modes but do not provide peak VRAM or host RAM.

topic: StepVideo A100-80 capacity edge and multi-GPU reference
title: Step-Video-T2V official README
claims: Step-Video-T2V is a 30B model supporting up to 204 frames; a Turbo checkpoint uses inference-step distillation.
Official requirements report 78.55GB peak for 768x768x204f and 77.64GB for 544x992x204f at 50 steps; flash-attn times are 860s and 743s respectively and 80GB is recommended.
Best-practice settings are 30–50 steps for base and 10–15 for Turbo, both at 204 frames; single-GPU quantization is delegated to DiffSynth-Studio.
Step-Video-TI2V adds 102-frame image-to-video, motion score and camera control, but its README states single GPU can take longer and requires CPU offload for high-resolution.

resources.gpu: 80GB recommended; official table tested on four GPUs

limitations: The official benchmark was on four GPUs and is high-resource evidence. A nominal 80GB GPU recommendation alone does not establish single-A100 High RAM qualification; 78.55GB peak is near the A100-80 capacity edge. No direct L4 or A100-40GB qualification.

title: gguf-org LTX-2.3 GGUF card
claims: The card provides an LTX-2.3 22B dev IQ4_XS GGUF and a q4_0 text projection, plus a universal FP8 E4M3 checkpoint for ComfyUI setup.
The model file sizes listed are IQ4_XS 14.8GB and IQ4_NL 15.4GB; the card states this is a GGUF quantization of Lightricks/LTX-2.3 and gives no hardware/time benchmark.
The card says no extra node is required under its described ComfyUI setup but warns that protobuf may be needed for a GGUF Gemma encoder.

resources.workflow: ComfyUI native LTX-2.3 with GGUF diffusion model

limitations: No L4/A100 run, VRAM peak, host RAM, speed or quality comparison; IQ file size cannot be treated as VRAM requirement.

topic: LTX-2.3 official Comfy quant formats and high-GPU measurement
title: Comfy-Org LTX-2.3 quantization documentation
claims: The LTX-2.3 exporter supports FP8 E4M3/E5M2, MXFP8, NVFP4, INT8 W8A8 and INT8 tensorwise; MXFP8/NVFP4 require Blackwell SM>=10 while INT8 tensorwise requires SM>=7.5.

On an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell with 512²x49 frames + audio, 20 Euler steps, the table reports BF16 46.1GB artifact/53.7GB peak/2.37 it/s; FP8 E4M3 29.1GB/36.7GB/2.27 it/s; NVFP4 21.7GB/29.6GB/1.56 it/s; INT8 tensorwise 29.2GB/38.6GB/2.73 it/s.
The same run reports video PSNR versus BF16 of 38.5dB FP8, 38.3dB MXFP8, 32.1dB NVFP4 and 45.4dB INT8 tensorwise; output contains 49 frames and FLAC audio.

resources.workflow: stock ComfyUI exporter and native LTXAV nodes

limitations: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell is outside requested L4/A100 boundary; values are not extrapolated. PSNR is a source-reported metric for the cited setup, not a broad visual evaluation.

title: city96 LTX-Video GGUF card
claims: The card is a direct GGUF conversion of Lightricks/LTX-Video, not a finetune, and is intended for ComfyUI-GGUF.
For 2B parameters it lists Q3_K_S 0.985GB, Q4_K_M 1.42GB, Q5_K_M 1.56GB, Q6_K 1.72GB, Q8_0 2.17GB and BF16/F16 3.94GB.
limitations: No target-GPU VRAM/time or output-quality benchmark; file size alone cannot establish a runnable video configuration.

title: HunyuanVideo-1.5 ComfyUI community timing report
claims: A user reports official 720p I2V FP16 workflow without upscale taking about 1.5 hours for a 5-second clip at 50 steps, with about 110 seconds per step; 480p was roughly twice as fast.
Replies recommend 4/8-step LightX2V LoRA and 848x480 starting sizes, but those replies do not give a reproducible paired hardware/VRAM/MP4 record.

resources.gpu: RTX5080 (post author); commenters mention RTX2060 Super/3090

limitations: A community failure/slow report with no attached reproducible package; RTX5080 is outside target hardware and should not be generalized. Replies mix configuration advice with other model discussions.
